title: When an eroding landscape has a steady shape
oneLine: A constructive local uniqueness theorem links erosion, diffusion and drainage on nonradial domains, with a separate radial theory and channel audit.
abstract: This analytical candidate studies a landscape whose elevation and downhill drainage must be solved together. Small erosion admits steady states on general smooth domains; constant forcing and a strict flow-growth margin give a locally unique branch with a convergent nested construction and explicit error budgets. Ellipsoids satisfy the geometric margin. A radial theory classifies steady states, relaxation and singular limits. A separate companion supplies wet–dry benchmarks and conditional channel-constraint obstructions. Neither manuscript establishes arbitrary-erosion nonradial existence or general wet–dry evolution.

narration:
Can a landscape reach a steady shape while rain keeps draining down its slopes? The difficulty is that the shape controls the water routes, while those routes control erosion. Both must be solved together.

This research candidate studies a mathematical model balancing uplift, diffusion and stream-power erosion. When erosion is sufficiently weak, it constructs steady landscapes on general smooth domains. Under additional assumptions, including constant forcing and a geometric margin, it proves that the nearby steady landscape is unique within a specified drainage class. Ellipsoids satisfy that geometric condition.

The construction alternates two steps: finding a drainage multiplier along uphill trajectories, then solving an equation for the elevation. A new error budget explains how inaccuracies in those steps affect convergence. It does not yet provide a certified numerical solution for the illustrated ellipse.

For circular or spherical domains, the paper goes further. It describes steady radial shapes for all positive parameter values and classifies what happens as diffusion becomes small. A summit may remain finite or grow without bound, depending on the erosion exponents. Those are predictions of this model, not measurements of real terrain.

A separate companion gives exact wet and dry benchmarks and identifies a compatibility condition in a channel model. Matching the initial integral and edge flow is not enough in the regular evolution class studied. The broader channel conjecture remains open.

The archive includes both papers, editable sources, exact identities, numerical checks and a response to the supplied audit. This is an unrefereed candidate; priority and the analytical arguments still require specialist scrutiny.

This is Evidence Press, dated the sixth of October twenty twenty-six. The papers and evidence are linked on the release page. This synthetic AI voice is an explanation, not additional scientific evidence.
